generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers 1..N per table, unique, never NULL; parent tables filled before children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from parent key pool; allow NULL where column nullable; include parent rows without children and child rows with NULL FK.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform in [min, max] from statistics, rounded to 2 decimals; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [min, max] from statistics; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Pick from a small pool of realistic values; include near-variants (case changes, one-character edits) of listed literals; allow NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Pick from a pool of realistic car names; include near-variants of listed literals; allow NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_small: Pick uniformly from the listed enum values; allow NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; share follows compact database null_rate (0.0 here, so plant a small share 5-10% to satisfy NULL targets).
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_distinct: On DISTINCT-target columns, repeat values so duplicate share is 20-50%.
generic_sampling_rules.ties_order_limit: On ORDER-target columns, plant ties at rank 1 in both ASC and DESC directions.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_values: For each listed literal, generate the literal, one step below, one step above (numbers by step, text by near-variant).

targets.data.ID: parent rows without children; joins with price.ID, production.ID
targets.production.ID: parent rows without children; joins with data.ID, price.ID
targets.price.ID: parent rows without children; joins with data.ID, production.ID
targets.country.origin: parent rows without children; child NULL FK in production.country
targets.production.country: child rows with NULL FK; joins with country.origin

targets.production.model_year: tie at rank 1, ASC/DESC, tie on COUNT(*)

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: country IN (1, 2, 3) OR country IS NULL

generation_specification.uncertainty: Null rates are 0.0 in statistics but NULL targets require planted NULLs; small shares (5-10%) are used. Formula for displacement/cylinders > 30 is not stated as a formula because it holds only conditionally; it is covered by boundary targets. No date pairs exist. No calculated columns beyond foreign-key copies.

issues.evidence: Specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas lists country.origin IN (1,2,3) and country.country IN ('USA','Europe','Japan'), but the extracted atomic operations for country.origin include comparison_boundary targets [0,1,2] and country.country boundary targets ['USA','usa','Japan','japan']. The spec's per_column_exceptions also lists these boundary values, so the boundary pool (0, 2, and case variants) conflicts with the stated domain rule. The program (spec.py ENUMS) restricts origin to [1,2,3] and country to ['USA','Europe','Japan'], so the boundary literals 0 and 'usa'/'japan' are never actually generated.
issues.requested_revision: Designer should reconcile the boundary targets with the domain rules: either drop 0 from country.origin boundaries and 'usa'/'japan' from country.country boundaries, or relax the domain rule to admit them. As written, the boundary pattern for these columns is not satisfiable under the stated domain.

issues.evidence: Specification lists comparison_boundary targets for data.mpg [29999.9, 30000, 30000.1] and data.displacement [29, 30, 31], but the semantic rules require mpg > 0 and displacement > 0 with realistic ranges (RANGES in spec.py: mpg 1-60, displacement 60-500). The boundary literals 30000 for mpg and 29-31 for displacement are far outside the realistic domain and are only meaningful for the derived expression displacement/cylinders > 30. The spec's own uncertainty note acknowledges this ('Formula for displacement/cylinders > 30 is not stated as a formula because it holds only conditionally').
issues.requested_revision: Designer should clarify that these boundary literals are for the derived expression, not the base column, and either add the expression as a formula or remove the misleading base-column boundary targets. The program currently injects 30000 into mpg and 29-31 into displacement via the boundary pool, which violates the realistic range intent.

issues.evidence: spec.py _sample_scalar applies plan['boundaries'] with 20% probability for any column with boundaries, including data.mpg (boundaries 29999.9/30000/30000.1) and data.displacement (29/30/31). This produces mpg values ~30000 and displacement values ~30, contradicting RANGES (mpg 1-60, displacement 60-500) and the semantic rules mpg>0, displacement>0 in spirit. Execution feedback shows data rows added (214) but does not report value ranges, so this is a latent domain violation.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer should gate boundary injection so that boundary literals outside the column's declared range are not sampled for the base column (or only used for the derived expression). Alternatively, the designer should remove those boundary targets from the base columns.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback nullable_columns shows 'country.country: generated rows: NULL 0 / 60' and 'price.price: generated rows: NULL 0 / 214' (and several data.* columns NULL 0). The NULL rule requires at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance. spec.py sets null_share only for NULL_TARGETS = ['production.country','data.car_name']; other nullable columns get null_share 0.0 and thus never receive NULLs. Per instruction 7 this is noted for the engineer and does not block a pass, but it is a deviation from the stated NULL rule.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer should extend NULL_TARGETS (or the null_share logic) to cover all nullable columns reported by the schema, so each nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance, following the compact null share.

issues.evidence: spec.py _sample_column for PK columns returns sequential integers starting after the compact max (pk_start). For data.ID and price.ID this yields fresh IDs, but the specification's comparison_boundary targets for data.ID/price.ID [14,15,16] and production.ID [14,15,16,380,381,382,383] are never generated because PK sampling bypasses the boundary pool. The boundary pattern for these PK columns is therefore unimplemented.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer should either generate boundary PK values (where they do not collide with compact rows) or the designer should confirm that PK boundary targets are satisfied by the compact rows themselves (IDs 14-16 exist in the compact data). If the latter, document it; otherwise implement boundary injection for PKs.

issues.evidence: Specification's ties_for_order_limit for country.country requires 'tie on AVG(country.country)' — an aggregate over a text column, which is not meaningful in SQLite (AVG of text yields 0.0). The program's TIE_COLS includes country.country and plants a tie value, but the tie semantics (AVG of text) are ill-defined.
issues.requested_revision: Designer should clarify the intended tie semantics for country.country (e.g., tie on COUNT(*) or on the text value itself) so the engineer can implement a meaningful tie.

unresolved_checks: Whether boundary literals for data.mpg (30000) and data.displacement (29-31) actually appear in generated rows was not directly verified from execution feedback (only row counts reported); the code path suggests they can appear with ~20% probability.
Whether PK boundary targets (data.ID/price.ID 14-16, production.ID 380-383) are considered satisfied by compact rows was not confirmed by the designer.

The construction_pairs summary reports 75/284 separated with no per-group breakdown; it is unclear which patterns remain unseparated, but per instruction 4 a missing separation alone does not establish an error.
